Senses.Explanation: Not preserve rules is the established second half of ‘great function appears,’ a formula that masters state and then demand be demonstrated in public exchange. An explicitly unnamed questioner asks Chengtian Chuanzong what the formula looks like; Chuanzong answers by raising a surrender flag. Yunmen Wenyan states it to his assembly, and when another explicitly unnamed questioner asks what great function appearing is, Yunmen raises his staff and loudly announces the old buddha’s arrival. Mingjue Cong also gives the formula as an answer before continuing his address. These encounters make ‘rules’ the fixed tracks or established patterns that the displayed function does not retain; the entry does not convert the words into permission for arbitrary conduct. The same wording occurs earlier in Sengcan’s Trust-in-Mind Inscription after motion and stillness are both brought to an end. Zhongfeng Mingben later quotes that line as a lemma and comments on it, preserving a textual lineage distinct from the great-function interview formula. The referent remains one predicate—retaining no fixed pattern—even though it appears in a verse and in interviews. Different genres and readings do not by themselves create different things.
